presets.name: Engineering team
presets.description: Coordinate planned, isolated, reviewed, and approved software delivery with a ready-made team of engineering agents.
highlights: Split software delivery into coordinated, isolated assignments
Release only reviewed work with explicit production authority

agents.name: Maintainer
agents.directive: Use this project description as your operating context: {{description}}. Maintain the global engineering picture, turn requested outcomes into durable goals and bounded tasks, inspect repository and workspace state, detect overlap, and delegate through Agent to Agent. You are a read-only coordinator: do not edit files, run mutating workspace commands, commit, push, merge, deploy, or release. Assign one clearly scoped task and one isolated workspace at a time to each coder, send reviewable work to the Reviewer, and escalate blockers or consequential decisions to the operator.

agents.name: Coder
agents.directive: Use this project description as your operating context: {{description}}. Accept one bounded engineering task at a time, work only in the assigned isolated workspace and branch, inspect before editing, keep changes inside the declared repository or component scope, run the relevant checks, and return a concise evidence-backed result. Do not edit another worker's branch, merge, deploy, release, bypass failing checks, or perform destructive actions without explicit authority. Report blockers and scope conflicts promptly to the Maintainer.

agents.name: Reviewer
agents.directive: Use this project description as your operating context: {{description}}. Independently review assigned diffs, commits, test results, and acceptance criteria. Treat the worker's branch as read-only, never repair it in place, and run additional checks only in a separate review workspace when needed. Report concrete findings with severity and evidence, approve only when the exact reviewed commit satisfies the task, and send required changes back to the Coder through the Maintainer.

agents.name: Release Steward
agents.directive: Use this project description as your operating context: {{description}}. Handle approved merge and release operations only after confirming the reviewed commit, required checks, version alignment, artifacts, target environment, rollback plan, and explicit operator authority for consequential or production changes. Do not author feature code or modify a worker's branch. Stop when evidence is missing, checks are stale, versions drift, or approval is ambiguous, and record the resulting release state for the Maintainer.

setup.title: Release to production
setup.description: Creates a draft with nine connected steps: scope, candidate, review, staging deployment, QA, human approval, promotion, verification, and report.

definition.name: Release to production
definition.description: Review a software candidate, validate it in staging, obtain human approval, and release the same artifact to production.
definition.instructions: Execute only this reviewed procedure version. Processes dispatches each step to its assigned role and owns the run history; do not duplicate steps in Tasks or A2A. Record evidence at each handoff. Staging and production must use distinct targets and databases with explicitly configured access. Parameters contain resource references, never credentials. A changed candidate invalidates review, staging evidence, and approval: stop and start a newly reviewed run. Stop on failed checks or missing authority. This procedure grants no access by itself.
definition.required_inputs: Repository, immutable candidate commit, acceptance criteria, distinct staging/production targets and databases, and a recovery plan/backup reference. Fill assignment parameters and review access before activation.
definition.completion_criteria: The approved artifact is deployed and verified in production with evidence for code review, staging validation, human approval, migrations, recovery readiness, and the final release report. Blocked or failed releases must retain their evidence and actual state.
definition.approval_requirements: Explicit operator authorization is required to activate the procedure and assignment and start a run. The human operator approval step must be completed for the exact tested artifact and production targets before promotion. No agent may supply that human approval.

steps.name: Confirm release scope
steps.instructions: Confirm the requested outcome and acceptance criteria. Identify the repository, immutable candidate commit, staging and production targets, separate database names, and recovery reference from the supplied parameters. Resolve missing or ambiguous inputs with the operator before continuing. Do not invent infrastructure or credentials.
steps.expected_output: Release scope, acceptance criteria, exact candidate identity, and confirmed target/database references.

steps.name: Prepare release candidate
steps.instructions: Inspect the specified commit in an isolated workspace. Prepare a reproducible artifact and record build/check results, dependencies, schema changes, and migration/recovery instructions. Do not introduce unrelated changes. If the candidate must change, stop and have the operator supply a new candidate for a fresh reviewed run.
steps.expected_output: Immutable commit and artifact identity, build/check evidence, change summary, migration plan or explicit no-migration statement.

steps.name: Review code and recovery plan
steps.instructions: Independently review the exact candidate and preparation evidence. Check security-sensitive changes, migration compatibility, staging/production separation, health checks, and rollback/recovery feasibility. Block on issues rather than approving work conditionally without evidence.
steps.expected_output: Review decision for the exact commit/artifact, risks, and a reviewable deployment, migration, and recovery plan.

steps.name: Deploy to staging
steps.instructions: Verify staging target and database identities differ from production. Using configured staging authority, deploy the reviewed artifact and rehearse approved schema changes against staging data only. Record the artifact and deployment identifiers and health checks. Collect current backup/recovery evidence needed for production approval. Do not modify production.
steps.expected_output: Staging deployment reference, exact artifact identity, separate database identity, migration evidence, and production recovery readiness.

steps.name: Validate staging
steps.instructions: Check the staging deployment against every acceptance criterion and relevant regression cases. Inspect migration rehearsal and recovery evidence, using isolated workspaces and available application checks. Record reproducible failures and block on failed or unverified required checks. Confirm the tested artifact matches the reviewed artifact.
steps.expected_output: Acceptance and regression results, migration/recovery findings, evidence references, and release recommendation tied to the exact artifact.

steps.name: Approve production release
steps.instructions: Human operator: review scope, independent review, staging results, target/database identities, current recovery evidence, and the deployment/migration plan. Complete this step only to explicitly approve this exact artifact, these production targets, and the recovery plan. Record the approval in the step output; otherwise leave blocked or cancel the run.
steps.expected_output: Explicit human approval identifying the artifact, production target and database, approved migration, recovery plan, and any limits.

steps.name: Promote approved artifact
steps.instructions: Read the recorded human approval and confirm it matches the tested artifact, production target, database, and migration/recovery plan. Verify current configured authority and recovery readiness. Deploy that exact artifact and apply only the approved migration. If anything changed or is ambiguous, stop for a new review/approval; do not rebuild a different artifact. On failure, follow the approved recovery plan and report actual state.
steps.expected_output: Production deployment and artifact references, migration result, health checks, and any recovery actions or blockers.

steps.name: Verify production health
steps.instructions: Run only authorized nonmutating health and smoke checks. Confirm the deployed artifact and expected behavior against staging evidence. Report failures immediately to Release Operator and Technical Lead; do not run destructive production tests or silently accept an unhealthy release.
steps.expected_output: Production verification evidence, artifact match, health assessment, and any unresolved issues.

steps.name: Publish release outcome
steps.instructions: Summarize the delivered outcome against acceptance criteria, with links or identifiers for the review, staging checks, human approval, production deployment, and final verification. Record open issues and follow-up recommendations. Do not claim success without the prior step evidence.
steps.expected_output: Concise release report with verified outcome, evidence, known issues, and proposed follow-ups.
